body:
How did you upload those file?  Were they uploaded with rclone?

The `#` character is a reserved character for onedrive business so rclone translates it back and forth into a unicode lookalike `＃`.

However it isn't a reserved character for plain onedrive so rclone probably shouldn't be translating it for onedrive backends not onedrive business backends...
I didn`t upload the folder with rclone, i make some tests and with i use # on destination folder works fine

@Cnly and @B4dM4n what are your thoughts on this?

Should we remove `#` from the translation for onedrive personal?
This issue is similar to https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/2913. Maybe they should be looked into together.

#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?
On the OneDrive (personal) backend files or directories with the `：` character cause issues with sync.  This is a unicode look-alike character for the standard colon `:`.  I use a program that auto-replaces a standard colon with the unicode `：` in some of my file and directory names and these files are causing problems.

I searched and found these issues that seem related, and I may just be hitting the same thing they are.
- https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/2920
- https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/2913
- https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/2633

Is my best option to just rename all my files to either use a regular colon `:` or not use either character at all?

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)
Reproduced using both latest stable and beta versions.

```
rclone v1.47.0
- os/arch: linux/amd64
- go version: go1.12.4

rclone v1.47.0-015-gaba15f11-beta
- os/arch: linux/amd64
- go version: go1.12.4
```

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (eg Windows 7, 64 bit)
Debian 9.8 64-bit


####  Which cloud storage system are you using? (eg Google Drive)
OneDrive Personal


#### The command you were trying to run (eg `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)
`rclone -vv sync test/ onedrive:test/`


#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag (eg output from `rclone -vv copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

I created a test directory with the following files:

ethan@nas:~$ rclone tree test

issue.title: WIP: handle special filenames on various backends

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
#### What is the purpose of this change?

This ist the follow up of #2955. It uses the `lib/encoder` package to translate filenames on backends with a restricted set of usable characters.

It defines the set of all available backend encodings in `fs/encodings/encodings.go` and updates the existing backends to use them.

As a quick test the change also includes a new flag for `rclone mount`, `--vfs-name-encoding`, which can be used to change the mounted filenames. For example setting `--vfs-name-encoding=local-windows` on a Linux platform will encode all special Windows filename characters and allow the mount to be shared via SMB to Windows clients with all filenames readable.

Backends completed:

 - [x] box
 - [x] drive
 - [x] dropbox
 - [x] jottacloud: changes the set of replaced characters, based on tests with `rclone info`
 - [x] local: includes a rewrite of path cleaning on Windows. Should be equal to the old implementation, but much simpler to read.
 - [x] onedrive
 - [x] opendrive

Backend encoding added as determined by the last test, but not implemented:

 - [x] s3: should not require to encode CTL and invalid utf-8 bytes
 - [x] pcloud
 - [x] mega
 - [x] b2

I'm currently not sure if the documentation is detailed enough to explain the mechanics. Any help to improve it is welcome.

This PR is not meant to merged as one, but as a central issue to track the progress.
Otherwise it should be ready to be tested.
It is available as a beta under (https://beta.rclone.org/branch/) with name like `v1.47.0-???-g????????-filename-encode-beta`.

#### Was the change discussed in an issue or in the forum before?

Fixes:

- [x] Invalid characters in the Local File System cause rclone copy and sync to re-download existing files - [x] under the new name #2633
- [x] Look-alike character `：` causes OneDrive remote files to be deleted on sync #3128
- [x] Onedrive file with "～" character in name is incorrectly read as "~" #2913
- [x] Error when copying file that contains a semicolon ";" #2750
- [x] Handling Control Characters #1580
- [x] special character in google drive #3083
- [ ] Copy Folders With # character Dosen't Work #2920

body:
@ncw @Cnly @felipe-negri
This issue has been probably solved by recent improvements in filename encoding and needs a retest

This should have been fixed by by #4909. A beta version has been uploaded here: https://beta.rclone.org/branch/onedrive-dont-encode-hash-percent/v1.54.0-beta.5038.2aed3d595.onedrive-dont-encode-hash-percent/. Any help with the testing would be appreciated!
